target_customer: Agencies and productized service businesses (creative, design, development shops) that sell recurring or one-time services to clients
problem: Agencies juggle separate tools for selling, billing, client portals, task intake and design feedback, none built around the client relationship.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for agencies, with a free tier until the first client and lifetime deals run through a deal marketplace
product_category: Agency operations platform (client portal, billing, project management)

founders.name: Masud (Mas) Hossain
education: Emergency medicine residency (physician); degree and school not stated in the sources opened
previous_startups: Sense a Life, COO and co-founder (reminder product for caregivers to remove a child from a car)
A bootstrapped startup he says reached an eight-figure exit in 3.5 years (unnamed on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page: physician-engineer who has coded since age 10. Founder-interview piece: cancer research at the University of South Fla., co-founder and president of Modern Village Project (nonprofit for village schools in Bangladesh), ran a one-person web agency in high school. Later building casehealth.ai with Fadi Shamma per the YC bio.

founders.name: Jean-Philippe Gagnon
founders.role: Co-founder (listed under Former Founders on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A portal, billing and task workflow product built on standard web tooling and payment integrations by a small team; the hard part was breadth of features, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Agencies that run billing and client portals through one tool face some switching cost, but the product category had many similar tools and features were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The founder interview says agencies stitched together generic tools such as Trello and PayPal; no incumbent was reported buying or copying Queue.

market_need_then: The founder interview says agencies assembled many generic tools that lacked a client focus, and that the team moved from esports coaching to agencies shortly before YC after judging coaching too small.

branding.domain_note: Operates at usequeue.com, a use prefix rather than the exact queue.com (observed on the live site in 2026).

identity.logo: White wordmark logo on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, friendly, benefit-first headlines such as Run your agency with 1 platform and Free until your first client

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch drew little attention (3 upvotes per a tracker); a lifetime-deal launch and a 5-star G2 rating are shown on the company site.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic dictionary word shared with many unrelated companies and trademarks, with no mascot or press about the brand; some customers praise support.

pivots.to: Platform for creatives and service businesses (agencies)
pivots.why: The team decided the esports coaching market was too small; this happened shortly before YC per the founder interview.

outcome_analysis: Queue is marked Inactive in the YC directory, but its website in 2026 shows a live product, a status page, apps and a new AI website builder, and no shutdown or sale was found, so the YC status and the live site conflict. The team pivoted from esports coaching to agencies just before YC and raised a small angel pre-seed, so what is documented is a bootstrapped-style company whose outcome cannot be classified from public sources.
notes: YC page says founded 2021; CB Insights says 2019; the founder interview describes work before YC, so 2019 is used with that conflict noted. No shutdown found despite Inactive status, so exit is unknown. A startupintros entry titled Queue seed $1M (2020-09-01) lists crypto investors and was judged to be a different company, so it is excluded. Competitor list is empty: searches for dated 2020 rivals (client portal and productized service tools) returned only 2026 pages, and the founder interview named no direct competitors. Cause of YC Inactive status is not public.
